questions.q: Which languages does Microsoft ship official, first-party Cosmos DB SDKs for?
options: .NET, Java, Python, and Node.js
Only .NET
Only Python and R
PHP and Ruby only
questions.explain: These four are the official, actively-maintained Microsoft SDKs referenced in the lesson; other languages rely on community SDKs.

questions.q: What two pieces of information does a Cosmos DB client need to connect to an account?
options: An endpoint URI and a key
Only a database name
A username and password pair only
Just the container name
questions.explain: The endpoint URI (the account's HTTPS address) plus a key together authenticate and route the client, playing the role a connection string plays for SQL Server.

questions.q: Why should an application create exactly one CosmosClient and reuse it, rather than creating a new one per request?
options: CosmosClient is expensive to construct — it opens connections, discovers regions, and initializes caches
Cosmos DB only allows one CosmosClient to ever be created per Azure subscription
Creating multiple clients is free but causes data corruption
There is no real cost difference either way
questions.explain: Constructing a CosmosClient does real setup work, so it should be a singleton reused across the application's lifetime, similar to pooling a database connection.

questions.q: What is a 'point read' in Cosmos DB?
options: Reading a single item by its id and partition key — the cheapest, fastest operation available
A query that scans every item in a container
A write operation that updates every document matching a filter
A read that ignores the partition key entirely
questions.explain: A point read targets one item by id + partition key directly, typically costing around 1 RU for small documents — the cheapest operation Cosmos DB offers.

questions.q: How can a developer see exactly what an operation cost after calling the SDK?
options: The response exposes the request charge (RU cost) directly
They must estimate cost from a query execution plan, as in SQL Server
Cosmos DB does not expose per-operation cost information
Cost is only visible in the Azure billing portal, days later
questions.explain: Every SDK response includes the request charge for that specific operation, giving real-time cost visibility per call.
